notes: Services present in the image but disabled only by commenting out their init line: miniigd, skt, snmpd, tr069. The binaries are still on the device and remain reachable to anything that can execute a command.

No /etc/passwd in the image: local accounts, if any, are created at runtime or authentication is handled entirely inside the application, not by the C library. Any credential check therefore lives in a binary and must be found by reversing, not by reading a config file.

findings.why: init line commented out, binary still present in the image
each is a place where attacker-influenced data could reach a shell
toolchain predates the marker, so the kernel maps the stack executable; memory-corruption bugs need no ROP chain
each handler parses request parameters and is a candidate entry point

findings.detail: mkfs_time is implausible (2038-02-22T08:46:56+00:00); raw=0x802d2100. Byte-reversed it reads 0x00212d80, which is suspiciously close to the filesystem size - possibly a vendor build-script bug writing a size into this field.
image requires at least 3747842 bytes (3.57 MiB) of flash
findings.why: highest burnAddr + length across sections; use this to sanity-check the part marking before dumping
